about: Values that may be absent (docs/adr/0055): an optional int64 `due`, an optional text `title` and an optional value of `Status` `status`, held in variables, in the record `item` and in the list of records `items`, and carried by the payload of `due.set`. An absent value is `null` in a payload, in a variable, in a record's field and in the done data, and `null` stands only where the machine declares an optional value. `due` starts absent and `other` and `status` present. `due.read` reads each value only where a test proves it present: `days` is `due !== null ? due.value : 0`, `late` is `due !== null && due.value > 10`, `early` is `due === null || due.value < 3`, `following` is `!(due === null) ? due.value + 1 : 0`, `label` is 'untitled' for no title, 'due soon' for 'soon' (an <elseif>) and the title otherwise (the <else>), `plain` takes `status.value` where `status` is present, `kept` takes `item.due.value` where the record's field is present, and the <foreach> adds the present days of the list into `listed` and counts the absent ones in `missing`; `same` is `due === other`, `absent` is `null === due` and `statusDone` is `status === Status.done`, so two absent values are equal and an absent value equals no present one. `due.fallback` writes `title ?? 'none'` into `label` and then `due ?? (huge * huge)` into `days`: the default is evaluated only when `due` is absent, and then it overflows an int64, so the statement fails, error.execution is raised and `fallbacks` is not counted; with `due` present the default is never evaluated. A delivery of `due.set` that lacks the key `due` is refused: nothing is written and error.execution is raised. `relay` sends the three optional variables to the machine as `due.sent`, each a value or `null`; the transition whose `cond` proves the day present reads it, and the other writes -1. `due.clear` assigns `null` to `due`, `other`, `status` and the record's `due`. The final's done data carries `due`, `title`, `status` and `item.due` as optional values and `due ?? 0` as a number. Expected values are derived from the document, not observed from a backend.

steps.note: each variable starts at the value its expr names: `due` absent, `other` and `status` present, and the record's `due` and `status` absent
every read finds `due` and `title` absent: the tests pick the branch that does not read them, `status` is read where it is present, and an absent `due` equals no present `other`
`title` is absent, so its default is written; `due` is absent, so its default is evaluated, overflows, and the statement fails with the block: `days` and `fallbacks` keep their values
a delivery whose optional fields each carry a value: the variables, the record taken whole and the list hold them
every read finds the values present: 12 > 10, not 12 < 3, 12 + 1, the <elseif> for 'soon', the variant, the record's day, and the list's one present day
both values are present, so neither default is evaluated: nothing fails and the block runs to its end
a delivery that carries `null` for a field makes it absent: in the variables, in the record and in the list's second record

`due` is absent again; the title is neither absent nor 'soon', so the <else> reads it; `status` and the record's day are absent, so `plain` and `kept` keep their values; the list holds one present day and one absent
a delivery that lacks the key `due` is no absent value: the first revision declares the field, so the delivery is refused, error.execution is raised and nothing is written
the absent day and status cross a send as `null` and the title as its text: the transition that proves the day present is not taken, the other writes -1
a third record fills the list to its capacity of three
7 is neither > 10 nor < 3; the <else> reads 'next'; the list's present days are 12 and 7; `due` equals the present `other` it holds the value of
the present day crosses the send as its number and is read where the `cond` proves it present
`null` assigned to three variables and to the record's day; the title and the record's other fields keep their values
two absent values are equal; `status` and the record's day are absent, so `plain` and `kept` keep their values; the list is as it was
the final's done data carries the absent values as `null`, the title as its text, and `due ?? 0` as "0": an int64 crosses as the text of its digits
